newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ITC looks at suits from Mexico under NAFTA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ITC looks at suits from Mexico under NAFTA.

text.p: The U.S. International Trade Commission said Wednesday it is weighing whether suits and jackets from Mexico made with interlinings of non-domestic fabric should be allowed in the United States duty free.

The ITC said it was responding to a letter from the U.S. Trade Representative's office saying that U.S. textile and apparel companies expressed concern about losing a domestic supply of some interlinings used in the assembly of men's, women's and children's suits and jackets in Mexico.
Under the rules of the North American Free Trade agreement, those clothes could not enter the United States duty free without U.S.-produced interlinings, the ITC said.

A provision of NAFTA provides for duty-free entry of garments from Mexico that were assembled wtih components made wholly of fabric formed and cut in the United States, the ITC said. The ITC said it will look at the probable effect of temporarily providing duty free entry for suits and jackets made with non-domestic interlinings and submit its opinion to the USTR by January 15.
